Definition
[Visual averaging of boundary vector fields] \group extensions Source: thurston:page-0302, thurston:page-0303

For $x\in H^3$, identify the sphere at infinity with the unit sphere in $T_xH^3$. For $y\in S^2_\infty $, let $i_{x,y}:T_yS^2_\infty \to T_xH^3$ be the induced identification. The visual average of a boundary vector field $X$ is \[ \operatorname {av}X(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi } \int _{S^2_\infty }i_{x,y}(X(y))\, dV_x(y), \] where $V_x$ is visual measure at $x$.
Proof

\sketch The visual identification transports every value of $X$ into the single vector space $T_xH^3$, so the normalized vector-valued integral is well-defined.

□
